page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-64xCPU-384GB is a Cloud Native virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. However, multi-core capabilities are robust, as demonstrated by a strong Passmark CPU score of 60061.44 and a strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 400.83 GB/sec. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong cached read bandwidth of 3728.41 GB/sec, while uncached read and write speeds remain average.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and lower single-core performance, this server is less suited for latency-sensitive, single-threaded tasks. However, its high core count and 384.0 GB memory capacity make it a cost-efficient option for highly parallelized workloads. It is well-suited for multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, where resource density and parallel execution offset the shared CPU model.
